Gizmos and scene markers

Stable Doppio Last updated: 2026-11-20

Move, rotate and scale handles for the selected entity, plus icons and frusta for lights, cameras, colliders and empties.

The viewport draws two overlays over the engine's render. Both are 2D canvases that rebuild the orbit camera's projection (uikit/components/viewport_math.rs), so they need no engine calls: they work from plain transform values and from component data the editor already reads.

Overlay Component Shows
Transform gizmo components/gizmo.rs the Move, Rotate and Scale handles of the selected entity
Scene markers components/scene_markers.rs lights, cameras, colliders and empties, which have no mesh to look at

Markers sit under the gizmo: a click goes to a gizmo handle first, then to a marker icon, then to the scene (orbit and mesh picking).

1. Transform gizmo#

Switch tools with 1 (Move), 2 (Rotate), 3 (Scale) while the pointer is over the viewport, or from the View menu. X over the viewport (or View > Snapping) turns snapping on: Move snaps to 0.25 m, Rotate to 15 degrees and Scale to 0.1, on the axis or plane being dragged only. The handle under the cursor lights up before you press it, and the one you are dragging turns yellow. Every drag is one undo step per handle.

Move (1)#

  • Axis arrows with shaded 3D cones and depth cueing: an axis pointing away from the camera is fainter, so the three arrows read as three dimensions instead of a flat cross.
  • Plane handles (the small squares between two arrows): drag inside the XY, XZ or YZ plane. The press ray is intersected with the plane, so the object follows the cursor exactly on that plane.
  • Movement is in world axes and writes the world position, so a child of a moved parent still follows the handle.

Rotate (2)#

  • Three rings on a translucent sphere. The half of each ring that is in front of the object is bright and thick, the half behind it is faint, which makes the orientation of every ring obvious.
  • While dragging, a wedge shows the swept angle and a label below the sphere shows the delta and the resulting angle (Y +37.5° → 62.5°).
  • The object turns the way the cursor goes from either side of the ring: the sign of the turn depends on whether the axis points at you or away from you (a positive rotation looks counter-clockwise when the axis points at the viewer, and screen angles run clockwise). It used to be a fixed sign, so the gizmo felt inverted from half of the viewing angles.

Scale (3)#

  • The axis handles follow the object's local axes, with shaded cube ends. A rotated object therefore scales along what you see; before, the handles were world-aligned while the scale is local, so dragging "X" on a rotated mesh scaled a different, invisible axis and looked broken.
  • The centre cube scales all three axes by the same factor (drag right or up to grow, left or down to shrink). The factor is exponential, so it never flips the sign and never reaches zero.
  • Values are clamped to 0.01 .. 1000.

For the texture side of scaling (a quad twice as big no longer stretches its material), see the UV scale section of the materials guide.

Edits#

The gizmo never calls the engine: it emits absolute edits and the app applies them.

Edit Applied as History key
Move { axis, position } world position gizmo:move:<id>:<axis>
MovePlane { plane, position } world position gizmo:move:<id>:<plane>
Rotate { axis, rotation } Euler degrees gizmo:rotate:<id>:<axis>
Scale { axis, scale } local scale gizmo:scale:<id>:<axis>
ScaleUniform { scale } local scale gizmo:scale:<id>:uniform

With snapping on, Edit::snapped(SnapSteps) rounds the edit before it is applied (the handle's own coordinates only, never negative zero, scale never below one step), so history keys and undo steps are unchanged.

2. Scene markers#

Lights, cameras and colliders are invisible in the render, so each gets a marker. Every marker has a faint stem to the ground and a small ground ring, so its height is readable, and a plate icon you can click to select the entity (the mesh raycast cannot hit them). Hover shows the name.

Entity Marker
Directional light a sun and a bundle of parallel rays along the real shining direction, plus a cross where the centre ray meets the ground. An unrotated sun uses the engine's default direction (0.35, -0.82, 0.45), exactly like the renderer.
Point light a bulb; when selected, the radius as a wire sphere and a soft shell
Spot light a bulb and the cone (angle and range); the range is capped at 6 m for unselected lights so long cones do not flood the view
Camera 3D a camera body with a lens, the frustum (field of view, aspect ratio, near and far) and the "up" triangle. Its size is fixed in the world (2.6 m deep): it does not grow or shrink as you fly around it, only its proportions follow the lens.
Collider 3D (selected only) the box, sphere or capsule with its offset and the entity's scale; triggers are orange and labelled
Empty entity a three-axis locator (red X, green Y, blue Z)
Point light (selected) Spot light (selected)
Camera (selected) Collider (selected)

Toggle: View > Hide / Show Scene Markers (editor.view.toggle_markers). The data is kept, so showing them again is instant.

How they are built#

scene_markers::collect walks the entities once and reads their components by name (Directional Light, Spot Light, Point Light, Camera 3D, Collider 3D, Light for the colour). It runs after every message that can change the scene (not on pointer moves or ticks), and measures about 6 ms for the 287 entities of dense_outdoor.caf. Orientation comes from the entity's local Euler angles, composed Rz * Ry * Rx like the engine; a directional light or camera under a rotated parent is therefore drawn with its local aim.

3. Why a scale or rotation edit could be ignored (fixed)#

An entity can carry the legacy Transform and the split Position 3D / Rotation 3D / Scale 3D components; scenes saved by older editors have both (the Chair project's cube, cylinder, sphere and camera do). The renderer and the hierarchy system build the world matrix from the split components whenever Position 3D exists, but the C ABI used to write rotation and scale only to Transform, and to read them from Transform first. The Inspector and the gizmos therefore showed the new number (Scale 47.159, 6.127, 9.381) while the object kept rendering with the old, unchanged Scale 3D: scale and rotation "did nothing", while position worked because it was already written to both.

Now (EngineAPI.cpp, prefersSplitComponents): reads report the components the renderer uses, and writes reach every component that is present, adding Rotation 3D / Scale 3D to a split entity that lacks them. Covered by entities_with_both_transform_and_split_components_render_their_scale_and_rotation (renders the entity before and after) and by a C ABI test (tests/test_capi.cpp).

4. For agents and scripts#

  • Query markers: whether they are visible and, per marker, the entity id, name, kind and world position.
  • Actions toggle_scene_markers, select_marker { id } (the same as clicking the icon) and toggle_gizmo_snap; the gizmo query reports snap.
  • Gizmo edits are ordinary Messages, so an agent can do no more than the UI.
  • Headless driver: fixture scene3d builds a small engine-backed scene (floor, cubes, sun, point and spot light, camera) and needs libcaffeine-capi; see headless-testing.md.

5. Limits#

  • The overlays use a 60° field of view and the orbit camera, like the viewport; a play-mode camera is not drawn through them.
  • Move is world-space only (no local / world toggle yet), Rotate adds to the Euler angles (it can hit gimbal lock). Snapping uses fixed steps (0.25 m, 15 degrees, 0.1); the steps are not editable in the UI yet.
  • Markers show a light's shape, not its colour or intensity numerically.
  • Orientation ignores parent rotation (see above).
  • Click-selection works on the icon only, not on the wire shapes.

6. Regenerating the images#

bash
cmake --build build --target caffeine-capi -j
./scripts/capture-gizmo-docs.sh        # headless screenshots of the scene3d fixture

The flow is caffeine-website/captures/flows/capture-gizmo-docs.json; it drives the real UI (hierarchy rows and the View menu) through the headless driver.
